question.content:
Boris wants to buy pineapples and watermelons. He wants to buy a total of at least $16$ fruits (condition $A$) with $\$60$ at most (condition $B$).

The graph represents the constraints on the number of pineapples $P$ and watermelons $W$ Boris buys.



[[☃ image 1]]

**Boris buys $6$ pineapples. How many watermelons can he buy to meet both his constraints?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

There is a solid line representing the inequality of the number fruit Boris wants to buy. This inequality goes through the points zero, sixteen and sixteen, zero. The shaded region for the inequality is above the line and is labeled a. There is another solid line representing the inequality for the amount of money Boris has to buy fruit. This inequality goes though the points zero, fifteen and twenty, zero. The shaded region for the inequality is below the line and is labeled b.

choices.content: At least $10$ watermelons and at most $12$ watermelons.
Boris doesn't have enough money left to buy any watermelons.
At least $16$ watermelons and at most $20$ watermelons.
